CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  August 18, 2025-5:00 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the regular meeting to order at 5:00 p.m.
  (Absent: Councilmembers hlampton and Jones)
  CLOSED SESSION  On the order of the Mayor, the regular meeting recessed at 5:00 p.m.
  to discuss the following closed session item:

  CITY COUNCIL CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL
  regarding pending litigation pursuant to Government Code
  Section 54956.9(d)(1)
  Name of Case: 615 S Catalina Ave LLC v. City of Pasadena, et
  aL
  Los Angeles County Superior Court Case No. 24STCP02861

  The above closed session item was discussed, with no reportable
  action at this time. The remaining closed session items were paused,
  with discussion to occur after the City Council's open session
  business was completed. See details below.

  On the order of the Mayor, the regular meeting reconvened at 6:07
  p.m. The pledge of allegiance was led by Congresswoman Laura
  Friedman.

  ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Rick Cole
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton (absent)
  Councilmember Justin Jones (absent)
  Councilmember Jason Lyon
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda

  Staff:  Acting City Manager Matt Hawkesworth
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

  SPECIAL ITEM  PRESENTATIONAL UPDATE BY CONGRESSWOMAN LAURA
  FRIEDMAN ON FEDERAL ISSUES, PROJECTS, AND
  PROGRAMS RELATED TO THE CITY OF PASADENA

  U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman provided an update on
  federal legislation and spoke on her legislative efforts to restore
  essential healthcare, advocate for fire resiliency, assist Eaton Fire
  victims, and implement identification requirements for federal
u  agents.

  Council Minutes  1  08/18/2025
   The City Council thanked Congresswoman Friedman for advocating
  for Pasadena and other essential federal legislation on various
  matters.

  Yadi, Pasadena resident, thanked Congresswoman Friedman
  for advocating for privacy policies and ethical technology.

  On order of the Mayor, and consensus of the City Council, the
  presentation was received and filed.

MATTERS NOT ON THE  crisis in Gaza and advocated for the City to divest from specific

  Rachel Wing, Pasadena resident, expressed concerns regarding
  recent federal immigration raids and urged the City Council to
  support State Senate Bill 805 (No Vigilantes Act).

  The following individuals advocated for the City Council to accept an
  invitation for a cultural exchange visit to Guanajuato, Mexico and/or
  provided comments related to forming a formal sister-city
  relationship with Guanajuato, Mexico:

  Rene Gonzalez, Pasadena resident
  Elvia Aragon, Pasadena resident
  Phillis Griffin, Pasadena resident

  In response to public comment, Councilmember Madison requested
  to agendize a proposal for a Sister City relationship with Guanajuato,
  Mexico for discussion.

  Adam Bray-Ali, Pasadena resident, expressed concerns regarding
  the funding model of the Pasadena Rental hlousing Board and the
  budget of the Rent Stabilization Department.

  Yadi, Pasadena resident, expressed concerns regarding safety and
  security matters related to the Tournament of Roses Rose Parade
  and the Rose Bowl Game.
